title: Buffett's 1978 letter: buying small stakes in great businesses cheaply, and why textiles earn poor returns
summary: Buffett explains how Berkshire's insurance float is put into concentrated stakes in outstanding businesses like SAFECO, bought below intrinsic value while corporations overpay for whole companies. He also shows why capital-intensive commodity businesses like textiles earn inadequate returns, and praises owner-minded managers.

principles.text: Commit heavily to stocks only when you understand the business, its prospects are good, management is honest and competent, and the price is attractive.
principles.quote: (1) businesses we can understand, (2) with favorable long-term prospects, (3) operated by honest and competent people, and (4) priced very attractively.

principles.text: Don't try to forecast short-term stock prices; it can't be done reliably.
principles.quote: We make no attempt to predict how security markets will behave; successfully forecasting short term stock price movements is something we think neither we nor anyone else can do.

principles.text: Concentrate holdings: when convinced, buy meaningful amounts rather than a little of everything.
principles.quote: Our policy is to concentrate holdings. We try to avoid buying a little of this or that when we are only lukewarm about the business or its price.

principles.text: Buying a small piece of a great business below 100 cents on the dollar beats paying premiums for mediocre companies in negotiated deals.
principles.quote: We paid less than 100 cents on the dollar for the best company in the business, when far more than 100 cents on the dollar is being paid for mediocre companies in corporate transactions.

principles.text: Undifferentiated, capital-intensive businesses earn poor returns unless supply is tight, because prices track operating costs, not capital employed.
principles.quote: producers of relatively undifferentiated goods in capital intensive businesses must earn inadequate returns except under conditions of tight supply or real shortage.

principles.text: Prize managers who think and act like owners, regardless of age.
principles.quote: It is a real pleasure to work with managers who enjoy coming to work each morning and, once there, instinctively and unerringly think like owners.
